newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.

text.p: *Volume narrows to 13.469 bln from 18.332 bln pesos
Manila overnight money was anchored at an average of 10.03125 percent on Tuesday amid high liquidity in the market, traders said.
Rates moved from 10.25 to 10.03125 percent, with 28 lenders and 18 borrowers.
"It's still very liquid," a foreign bank dealer said, despite the fact that banks bought a lot of the Central Bank's one-year T-bills last Monday.
Banks continued to be awash with liquidity from maturing reverse repos, traders said. But the Central Bank had placed a floor on rates through its overnight borrowing which is at 10.0 percent.
In the secondary market, banks opted to buy the three-month and six-month bills after the Central Bank lowered its borrowing rate on its one-year special series T-bills to 10.40 from 10.70 percent.
The Central Bank's action had pulled down the rate of comparative bills, they said.
A Reuter poll of seven financial institutions showed bid rates of 9.80 to 10.0 percent on the three-month bills, and 10.002 to 10.20 for the six-month bills.
